details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_findings_record.py:666, 698-701 (gemini cites 652-667) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: compute_reviewer_findings silently drops FLAGGED_BY entries that match no reviewer that ran (for example `reviewer_N` tokens or reviewers whose slot is not ok), so a finding with one matched reviewer plus one unmatched token counts as lone and then as lone_accepted or lone_rejected.
  WHY: This breaks the issue's definition of lone and the fragment's flagged_by_missing contract; flagged_by_missing fires only when no entry matches at all. All five reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/review_findings_record.py:588-592, 648-650 (glm also cites 120-128; scripts/review_parse_consolidator.sh:902-905) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: On a clean round the parser writes parse_failed=1 / parse_error=no_issue_markers, build_record adds consolidator_parse_failed, and every reviewer prints `outcome=unavailable reason=consolidator_missing` instead of all-zero lines.
  WHY: Converged final rounds never produce counted lines, so the per-reviewer "runs" column is too low and the unavailable count is inflated. All three rated it MAJOR.
- tests/test_review_chatgpt_findings_record.py:697-710, 750-770 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_three_fixture` and `test_reviewer_findings_lines_zero_findings` write an empty review_issues.txt but no parser_stats.txt, which is not what production writes for a clean round (parse_failed=1, parse_error=no_issue_markers).
  WHY: The test passes while production emits consolidator_missing unavailable lines instead of zeros.
- scripts/check_workflow_analysis_report.py:385-386 (.github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml:1622) | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The check `if REVIEWER_FINDINGS_MARKER.encode("utf-8") in raw: return 0` in insert_reviewer_findings searches the whole report, which is model stdout, so a model that emits the marker skips the code-built table with exit 0 and no warning.
  WHY: Model-written content under the marker gets published, which breaks the "code-built, never a model tally" rule; each run writes a fresh REPORT_FILE, so the check protects no real retry path. Severity disagreement: sonnet, minimax and glm rated it MAJOR, luna rated it NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/check_workflow_analysis_report.py:365 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The marker check `if REVIEWER_FINDINGS_MARKER.encode("utf-8") in raw: return 0` in insert_reviewer_findings searches the whole report content, so a model that outputs the marker makes the script skip table insertion with exit 0.
  WHY: The code-built table is replaced by whatever the model emitted. This is the same code as the line 385 finding above, but the cited line number is 20 lines away, so it is not merged.
- scripts/analyze_workflow_logs.py:338-395 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: aggregate_reviewer_findings uses the workflow_family == "review_autofix" check only to increment review_runs, and sums reviewer_findings entries from runs of any workflow family.
  WHY: REVIEWER_FINDINGS lines from other trusted runs (CI, or the analysis job's own tee'd log) inflate or forge reviewer totals, and runs_with_lines can exceed review_runs. All four rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:1789-1847 (gemini also cites 2031-2037; glm also cites ~2472-2475) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_reviewer_findings_from_full_logs` / `_apply_reviewer_findings_from_full_logs` parse REVIEWER_FINDINGS lines from every trusted-origin run, gated only on origin trust and not restricted to the review_autofix workflow family.
  WHY: Any same-repo trusted workflow that prints a matching line injects forged counts into the published Reviewer Findings table. All four rated it MAJOR.
- tests/test_analyze_workflow_logs.py:648-652 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_reviewer_findings_aggregate` is defined after the `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())` guard, so it never runs in CI's script-mode coverage run (.github/workflows/ci.yml:2978).
  WHY: aggregate_reviewer_findings gets no coverage in the CI coverage gate. Severity disagreement: gemini and glm rated it MAJOR, sonnet rated it NIT and noted the test still runs under the pytest-collected tests-system-python shards.
- tests/test_collect_workflow_logs.py:3740-3792 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_reviewer_findings_parsed_from_full_logs` (~3750) and `test_main_reviewer_findings_on_trusted_run_only` (~3792) are defined after the main guard at 3740-3741, so CI's script-mode run (.github/workflows/ci.yml:2971) never reaches them.
  WHY: Parsing and trust-gate logic go unexercised by the coverage gate. Severity disagreement: gemini and glm rated it MAJOR, sonnet rated it NIT.
- scripts/check_workflow_analysis_report.py:364 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: render_reviewer_findings_section says counts come from "{runs_with_lines} of {review_runs} review runs whose logs this analysis read", but review_runs counts every review_autofix run in the window, not only those whose logs were downloaded.
  WHY: The text hides how small the capped log sample is (--max-log-runs default 15). Rated NIT.
- scripts/review_findings_record.py:766-769 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fail-open wrapper around emit_reviewer_findings_lines in run_write prints `::warning::REVIEWER_FINDINGS outcome=failed reason=<ExceptionClass>` to stdout with a plain print, not as a real annotation on stderr.
  WHY: Operators grepping stderr will not see systematic emitter failures, which contradicts the agents.md fragment's promise. Rated NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "A run with no findings emits a line per reviewer with zeros." (Tests section of issue #10058)
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_findings_record.py compute_reviewer_findings / build_record; production-shaped fixture in tests/test_review_chatgpt_findings_record.py `_three_fixture` / `test_reviewer_findings_lines_zero_findings`
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: No hunk handles the parser's clean-round output, parser_stats.txt with parse_failed=1 / parse_error=no_issue_markers (scripts/review_parse_consolidator.sh:902-905). That output leads to consolidator_parse_failed (scripts/review_findings_record.py:591-592, 648-650), then consolidator_missing and unavailable lines. The zero-findings fixture writes an empty issues file without parser_stats.txt, so the tested path never occurs in production. No fixture asserts the "missing reviewer field → unavailable" path against parser_stats.txt-shaped consolidator output.
- requirement: The acceptance-gate tests (including `tests/test_collect_workflow_logs.py::test_reviewer_findings_parsed_from_full_logs` and `tests/test_analyze_workflow_logs.py::test_reviewer_findings_aggregate`) are marked "met", and "The analysis table is built from a fixture log" is covered by analyzer tests.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_collect_workflow_logs.py, tests/test_analyze_workflow_logs.py (script-mode CI runners in `.github/workflows/ci.yml:2971,2978`)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `tests/test_collect_workflow_logs.py:3750` and `:3792` are defined after `raise SystemExit(main())` at line 3741, and `tests/test_analyze_workflow_logs.py:652` is defined after the guard at line 649, so they never run in the script-mode coverage gates (--fail-under=45 / --fail-under=67). minimax rated this BLOCKER, luna rated it NIT.
- requirement: "The workflow log analysis adds a 'Reviewer findings' table to its report: per reviewer over the report window, runs, findings raised, lone findings, lone rejected (count and percent), lone accepted (count and percent)."
  expected_change_site: scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py log selection (select_notable_runs_for_logs / export_categorized_logs); scripts/analyze_workflow_logs.py aggregate_reviewer_findings; coverage sentence in scripts/check_workflow_analysis_report.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: Findings are extracted only for runs selected by select_notable_runs_for_logs (`scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:2426, 2475`). That selection is capped (--max-log-runs default 15) and favours failed, retried and slow runs (`scripts/collect_workflow_logs.py:1346-1450`), and export_categorized_logs covers only errors/slow/recent. The table therefore reports a small, biased sample rather than the whole window, and neither the diff nor the report text says so.
- requirement: "The workflow log analysis adds a 'Reviewer findings' table to its report: per reviewer over the report window, runs..."
  expected_change_site: scripts/analyze_workflow_logs.py aggregate_reviewer_findings; scripts/check_workflow_analysis_report.py render_reviewer_findings_section
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: Unavailable entries increment only the global counters and are skipped before a reviewer row is created or incremented (`scripts/analyze_workflow_logs.py:371-374`). The runs column counts only counted entries (`scripts/analyze_workflow_logs.py:380-382`), so unavailable reviewer runs are left out, and a reviewer with only unavailable lines gets no row.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/check_workflow_analysis_report.py:insert_reviewer_findings, line 385 (caller .github/workflows/workflow-log-analysis.yml line 1759; REPORT_FILE from line 1622) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The duplicate check looks for "<!-- reviewer-findings-table v1 -->" anywhere in a model-written file, so a model that copies the marker makes the script skip the code-built table, exit 0 and log no warning.
  WHY: The model's content is published, breaking the "never a model tally" rule. The check protects no retry path (lines 1478-1484, 1622 write REPORT_FILE fresh; line 1759 inserts once). Fix: drop the check or warn.
- scripts/review_findings_record.py:build_record lines 588-592; compute_reviewer_findings line 648; scripts/review_parse_consolidator.sh lines 902-905 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: On a clean round the parser writes parse_failed=1 / parse_error=no_issue_markers, so the record gets consolidator_parse_failed and every reviewer prints "outcome=unavailable reason=consolidator_missing" instead of zeros. test_reviewer_findings_lines_zero_findings passes only because _three_fixture never writes parser_stats.txt.
  WHY: Clean converged rounds never produce counted lines, so Runs is too low and the unavailable count is inflated. Fix: carry parse_error into the record and count no_issue_markers with an empty issues list as zeros; add a fixture.
- scripts/review_findings_record.py:compute_reviewer_findings line 666; lines 698-701 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A FLAGGED_BY entry that matches no reviewer that ran is dropped without a
summary: Reviewer consensus flagged 10 multi-reviewer item(s) across 15 total consensus item(s)
